2af622efa72377b1e25653ce1b1ec70b6f9cb1f0.title: [LV] Latvijas Banka is issuing a symbolic collector coin "Chestnut"
2af622efa72377b1e25653ce1b1ec70b6f9cb1f0.summary: On Thursday, 8 October, Latvijas Banka will issue "Chestnut", a silver collector coin with gilded details, symbolically depicting one of the heralds of autumn. The coin gives a new expression to a work by the artist who won Latvijas Banka's open design competition on the theme of nature last year. Chestnut trees were first introduced to Latvia around the turn of the 17th–18th centuries and were found mainly in the parks of manors. One of the great chestnut trees served as the inspiration for the prose masterpiece Straumēni by Edvarts Virza. Beneath the branches of the chestnut tree, the household and their guests are depicted celebrating or resting after a day's work. In the early 20th century, the renowned Latvian landscape painter Vilhelms Purvītis immortalised a grove of these trees in his painting Blooming Chestnut Trees . A small number of sweet chestnut trees ( Castanea sativa ) also grow in Latvia, mainly in Kurzeme. Figurines fashioned from chestnut fruits have become favourite playthings for children, and chestnuts are also believed to have healing properties. Carrying a chestnut in one's pocket is believed to protect against misfortune. For women, good fortune has traditionally been associated with a chestnut in the left pocket; for men, in the right. The chestnut coin is like a talisman, embodying all the positive qualities of the tree and its fruit. In Latvian, the word for chestnut tree is used in both the masculine ( kastanis ) and feminine ( kastaņa ) grammatical gender. This means that the tree, and now the coin, belongs to everyone. Yet the reasons for carrying it in one's pocket remain individual. The collector coin "Chestnut" was designed by artist Kaspars Līdums , who entered and won the 2025 design competition on the theme of nature with his design

ab2df0a89adfa9a08334fbc3cbd42589e66f1964.title: [VA] New numismatic issues, year 2025, of the Governorate of the Vatican City State
ab2df0a89adfa9a08334fbc3cbd42589e66f1964.summary: The Governorate of the Vatican City presents a new and significant selection of numismatic issues for the year 2025, an expression of faith, institutional continuity, and high artistic value. b7bc89674986a5b29fe51d6aa5d7facbe23af192.title: [VA] Three States, One Tribute to Saint Francis: the Numismatic Triptych Dedicated to the Canticle of the Creatures is born
b7bc89674986a5b29fe51d6aa5d7facbe23af192.summary: Italy, San Marino and the Vatican together Celebrate the Saint of Assisi Rome, 4 May 2026 – “The Canticle of the Creatures”, one of the most celebrated texts of European spiritual and literary tradition, takes center stage in a shared numismatic project involving the Italian Republic, the Republic of San Marino and the Vatican City State. The result is a triptych of copper coins with a nominal value of €0.75 each, conceived as a single narrative in three chapters dedicated to the work composed by Saint Francis of Assisi around 1224, considered the earliest known text of Italian literature whose author is known.
